2. Gratia Cooperans (Cooperating Grace): The healed will actively collaborates with God; the will is both moved and moving (voluntas mota et movens). Actual: aiding concrete good deeds. Habitual: serving as the enduring principle of merit.

🧠 Mnemonic: Mota vs. Mota et Movens: Operating turns the key; Cooperating drives the car together.

column1: Why does Operating Grace (Gratia Operans) not violate or coerce human free will?
column2:
Coercion occurs only when two finite agents compete externally on the same ontological plane. God, however, is the transcendent Creator of human freedom, more intimate to the will than the will is to itself (interior intimo meo).

When God moves the fallen will from sin to good, He does not force it mechanically from outside, nor merely entice it emotionally; He heals sin's paralysis from within, liberating freedom so man can finally choose his true good.

🧠 Mnemonic: Not External Rival, but Internal Creator: Grace heals the broken wing so the bird is free to fly.

column1: How did late-medieval Nominalism (Potentia Dei Absoluta vs. Ordinata) pave the way for Martin Luther's reformation theology?
column2:
Nominalists (Ockham, Biel) severed God's arbitrary omnipotence (potentia absoluta) from His wise established order (potentia ordinata), claiming God could arbitrarily save an unrepentant sinner without sanctifying grace or condemn one with charity.

Consequence: This broke the intrinsic ontological link between charity and salvation, turning grace into a mere external legal token. Luther inherited this framework, discarded created grace (habitus) altogether, and taught forensic justification (simul iustus et peccator).

🧠 Mnemonic: Arbitrary Will Breaks Ontological Grace: Nominalism detached grace from transformation; Luther threw out the empty shell.

column1: What was Martin Luther's 'Turmerlebnis' (Tower Experience) regarding 'Iustitia Dei' in Romans 1:17?
column2:
Initially, Luther read iustitia Dei (righteousness of God) as God's active, punitive justice demanding impossible fulfillment of the Decalogue, filling him with terror before an angry Judge.

In the Turmerlebnis, he reinterpreted iustitia Dei passively: as the merciful righteousness that God externally imputes to the believer solely through faith (sola fide), covering interior sinfulness.

🧠 Mnemonic: Active Judge -> Passive Cloak: From terrifying demand to external forensic cover.

column1: How does the Council of Trent (Session V, canon 5) refute Luther's identification of concupiscence with sin (Simul Iustus et Peccator)?
column2:
Luther equated post-baptismal concupiscence (fomes peccati) with sin itself, concluding that Baptism leaves guilt intact (simul iustus et peccator).

Catholic Dogma (Trent V, 5): Baptism truly erases everything having the proper nature of sin, infusing sanctifying grace. Remaining concupiscence is called 'sin' only analogically because it comes from sin and inclines to sin (ex peccato est et ad peccatum inclinat); resisted by grace, it is not sin, but an arena for virtuous combat.

🧠 Mnemonic: Temptation is Not Consent: The embers (fomes) remain for battle, but the fire of guilt is extinguished.

column1: Explain St. Augustine's maxim endorsed by Trent (Session VI, ch. 16) on Catholic merit: 'Cum Deus coronat merita nostra...'
column2:
'Cum Deus coronat merita nostra, nihil aliud coronat quam dona sua' ('When God crowns our merits, He crowns nothing other than His own gifts').

Between Creator and creature, strict commercial debt is impossible (ST I-II, q. 114, a. 1). Merit exists solely because God freely promised to reward what His own grace produces in His children (ordinatio divina). Thus, merit is not a bribe, but the filial growth of charity and capacity to enjoy God (frui Deo).

🧠 Mnemonic: Father Buying the Paint: A father gives his child paper and paints, guides his hand, and then proudly rewards the drawing.

column1: What are the four necessary conditions for a human act to possess supernatural merit before God (ST I-II, q. 114, aa. 2-4)?
column2:
1. Divine Ordination (Ordinatio Divina): God's free promise associating man with His grace;
2. State of Grace & Charity: Union with Christ the Vine (Jn 15:5: 'Apart from me you can do nothing');
3. Free Deliberate Act in Status Viae: Performed freely during earthly pilgrimage prior to death;
4. Right Intention / Offering: Directed to God in charity (fostered daily by the Morning Offering uniting work to Christ's priesthood).

🧠 Mnemonic: P-G-F-O: Promise of God, Grace/Charity, Free pilgrim act, Offering in Christ.

column1: Distinguish precisely between Meritum de Condigno and Meritum de Congruo (ST I-II, q. 114, a. 3).
column2:
1. Meritum de Condigno (Condign Merit): Merit in the strict sense, grounded in a proportional equality of justice conferred not by human strength, but by the dignity of Christ's grace and the Holy Spirit indwelling the soul. Merits an increase of grace and eternal glory.
2. Meritum de Congruo (Congruous / Fitting Merit): Merit in a broader sense, resting upon divine friendship and generosity rather than strict proportion (e.g. a mother meriting through prayer the conversion of a sinner, like St Monica for St Augustine).

🧠 Mnemonic: Proportion vs. Friendship: Condigno relies on Christ's proportion within you (for your glory); Congruo appeals to God's generous friendship (for others).

column1: Can any person merit First Justification (prima gratia) for himself de condigno (ST I-II, q. 114, a. 5)?
column2:
No. First justification cannot be merited de condigno by anyone prior to grace, because merit itself presupposes the state of grace and union with Christ (the effect cannot precede its own cause).

A sinner's prayer or repentance under actual grace disposes him fittingly for mercy, yet initial justification remains purely an unmerited, gratuitous gift of God's mercy.

🧠 Mnemonic: You Cannot Earn the Starting Line: A branch must first be grafted into the Vine before it can bear meritorious fruit.

column1: What is the Christological foundation of all Christian merit?
column2:
Our actions possess zero meritorious value if isolated from Jesus Christ. Because Christ's humanity is the supreme instrument of the Trinity (organum divinitatis), He alone merited our salvation de condigno in the absolute sense.

Through Baptism and charity, Christians are grafted into Christ's Mystical Body; thus, our daily labour, prayer, and suffering become living participations in Christ's own priestly and redemptive mediation.

🧠 Mnemonic: Grafted into the Vine: Human sap has no eternal worth unless flowing from Christ the Root.
